transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah. I guess the main reason I came in is that I feel like I sort of… flipped into this mode where I suddenly had to do everything, all at once.

I recently moved into a new apartment, and I was barely even settled in — like, there were still boxes around, I hadn’t figured out where half my dishes were going, normal life stuff was still kind of unfinished — and then all of a sudden I started saying yes to all these extra things. Mentoring sessions, extra client prototype work, and then I decided my entire portfolio needed to be redesigned immediately, like right now, like it was somehow urgent and if I didn’t fix it then I was wasting my life or falling behind.

It felt like I had to overhaul everything in one big sprint, if that makes sense. Like I couldn’t just unpack and get used to the apartment. I had to fix my work, my future, my whole direction — and I know that sounds dramatic, but that’s honestly how it felt.
Can you describe how this urge to do everything at once affected your sleep, your ability to sit still, or how much you were moving around or pacing?

Yeah, it really affected that. Sleep especially got weird because even at night, when I knew I should be winding down, I just… couldn’t. There were nights where I’d be in the apartment and instead of going to bed I’d start moving furniture around, like deciding the bookshelf was wrong or the desk needed to be angled differently, and then that would turn into labeling storage bins or reorganizing a closet.

And it wasn’t like, “Oh, I’m just being productive.” It felt more like if I stopped, something in me would start buzzing. I’d sit down for maybe a minute and then pop back up because I remembered another thing I needed to fix. I’d be tweaking mockups on my laptop, then pacing from room to room, then going back to the mockups, then realizing I should unpack something, then pacing again. It was hard to just be still.

I remember thinking, “Just go to sleep, you have to function tomorrow,” but my body didn’t really feel like it was taking that seriously. Stopping felt almost impossible, like I had to keep moving until everything was somehow done, even though obviously there was no way to finish all of it in one night.
Can you describe how you were feeling emotionally during this time? Were you feeling unusually high, excited, or irritable?

Yeah… emotionally it was kind of intense. Earlier this month I remember feeling almost electric, like really upbeat and charged, like everything seemed possible and I was suddenly the person who could just solve all of it if everyone would move fast enough.

But then it would flip really quickly. If there was even a small delay, I’d get irritated in a way that felt out of proportion. Like I snapped at a contractor because something about the apartment wasn’t happening on the timeline I had in my head, and at the time it felt completely justified, like they were blocking me from getting my life in order. And then with my sister too — she asked a pretty normal question, or didn’t respond as quickly as I wanted, and I reacted like she was deliberately slowing me down.

It’s embarrassing saying it out loud, because I don’t think they were doing anything terrible. It just felt, in the moment, like every tiny obstacle was personal, like people were standing in the way of this momentum I had. So yes, I was definitely more upbeat and excited than usual at points, but also really irritable, really quick to snap.

Can you recall if there was a distinct period when your mood was noticeably different from your usual self — like a clear shift where you felt unusually upbeat, energized, or irritable in a way that was out of character for you?

Yes, there was a pretty clear shift earlier this month. It wasn’t just “I’m in a good mood” or “I’m motivated today.” It felt noticeably different from my normal self, like I was almost electric — upbeat and charged, like everything had this urgency and possibility to it.

And then the weird part was how fast that could turn into irritation. One minute I’d feel energized and like I could handle everything, and then if something tiny slowed me down, I’d react like it was a much bigger deal than it was. I snapped at a contractor over a delay, and I got sharp with my sister too, over things that… looking back, were not that serious. But in the moment it felt like they were personally blocking me or getting in the way of what I needed to do.

So, yes, it did feel like a distinct period where I wasn’t quite myself — more upbeat, but also much more easily irritated than usual.
